report.summary: CoreDNS replicas were scaled down from 4 to 1 at 13:22, overloading the remaining replica and causing CPU saturation, request timeouts, and widespread DNS resolution failures (EAI_AGAIN) across the cluster, including notification-service calls to SMS and push vendors.

ranked_hypotheses.title: CoreDNS replica scale-down causes DNS resolution failures

supporting.note: CoreDNS scaled down from 4 to 1 replicas at 13:22, just before the incident onset.
CoreDNS CPU utilization spiked to 105.9% right after the scale-down.
CoreDNS logs show plugin/errors timeout querying external vendor endpoints.
notification-service logs EAI_AGAIN errors resolving sms-vendor.example.net starting at 13:25.
notification-service logs EAI_AGAIN errors resolving fcm.push-provider.example.com starting at 13:25.

contradicting.note: Errors are local DNS resolution failures (EAI_AGAIN) rather than HTTP/transport layer failures from the vendor.

facts.text: notification-service error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-14T13:25:00+00:00 and peaked at 26.58%.
CoreDNS replicas were scaled from 4 to 1 at 2026-10-14T13:22:00+00:00.
CoreDNS error rate and latency spiked starting at 2026-10-14T13:23:00+00:00.
notification-service logged EAI_AGAIN errors for sms-vendor and push-provider starting at 13:25.

assumptions: The reduction of CoreDNS replicas from 4 to 1 directly caused CPU saturation and packet/timeout drops under normal cluster DNS load.

timeline.event: CoreDNS scaled down from 4 to 1 replicas for cost optimisation
CoreDNS CPU and latency metrics spike
CoreDNS logs first UDP timeout error
notification-service logs first EAI_AGAIN DNS resolution failure

recommended_actions.action: Scale CoreDNS replicas back to at least 4
recommended_actions.rationale: Restores cluster DNS processing capacity and resolves CPU exhaustion and timeouts.

recommended_actions.action: Implement safety thresholds on infrastructure replica count changes
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents accidental or unauthorized critical infrastructure scale-down below high availability requirements.
